decision.decision: We can't fill this order from stock because CC-TEE-WHITE size S has 0 on hand. Accounting filed approval request #1 to pay overdue invoice 501 ($840.00) to Bulldog Print Co, because that open invoice is the only thing stopping the vendor from shipping. Once it's paid, we'll order 1x CC-TEE-WHITE S at $8.00. Draft 1 is ready to tell the customer about the delay.
decision.reasoning: The shop date is 2026-08-31. Inventory shows 0 units of CC-TEE-WHITE size S, and the ticket asks for 1, so we're 1 short. The restock vendor is Bulldog Print Co (vendor_id 1), with a 5-day lead time. That vendor has can_ship_new_product=false because invoice 501 ($840.00, due 2026-08-28) is still open and is now 3 days overdue. Accounting couldn't file the purchase order yet because the vendor is blocked. Checking holds $3,400.00 and nothing else is outstanding. Paying the invoice would leave $2,560.00, and the $8.00 tee would leave $2,552.00, so cash covers both. The tee costs $8.00 and lists at $28.00, a 71.4% margin. If request #1 is approved and the order goes in today, the earliest arrival is 2026-09-05. Each day the approval waits pushes that date back. Invoice 501 is described as 'Rush reprint CC-TEE-WHITE S', so that earlier reprint may already cover this unit.
next_steps: Owner: review and approve request #1 ($840.00, invoice 501) on the dashboard. Approving it pays the invoice automatically.
Owner: check whether the rush reprint on invoice 501 already covers this size S tee, to avoid ordering a duplicate.
Owner: review draft 1 to Tauhid Zaman and send it. It gives 2026-09-05 as the earliest arrival and makes no firm promise.
After the payment goes through, re-run ticket 101. Accounting will then file a purchase order for 1x CC-TEE-WHITE S from Bulldog Print Co at $8.00, which also needs approval.

After the purchase order is approved and placed, the ticket moves to waiting_on_vendor. The expected arrival is the order date plus 5 days. Customer Service will draft a follow-up with the confirmed date, and Inventory will reserve the unit when it arrives.

decision.decision: I'm offering the Yale AI Club 10% off: $52.20 per hoodie instead of the $58.00 list price, which is $1,044.00 for all 20. That leaves $30.20 profit per hoodie (57.9%). I set aside the 8 size M hoodies we have for this order. The other 12 are not promised and have no date, because we can't currently pay to restock them and our supplier is blocked by an unpaid bill.
decision.reasoning:
Each hoodie costs us $22.00 and lists at $58.00, so we make $36.00 (62.1%) at full price. Accounting priced three discounts for 20 hoodies: 5% is $55.10 each, $1,102.00 total, 60.1% margin. 10% is $52.20 each, $1,044.00 total, 57.9% margin. 15% is $49.30 each, $986.00 total, 55.4% margin. I picked 10% because it is a real bulk discount without giving away more than needed. 15% is my ceiling if the club pushes back.

Stock: we had only 8 size M hoodies (Aisle A) and Inventory has now set all 8 aside for this ticket, so 12 are missing. The hoodie supplier, Bulldog Print Co (5-day lead time), won't ship anything new while invoice 501 ($840.00, due 2026-08-28) is unpaid and 3 days overdue.

Cash: checking holds $3,400.00. $3,240.00 is already waiting for your approval: request #1 pays invoice 501 ($840.00, ticket 101) and request #2 pays rent ($2,400.00, due 2026-09-02, ticket 102). If both are paid, $160.00 is left. Accounting estimates a 12-hoodie restock at $264.00 (12 × $22.00), so we would be $104.00 short. The system doesn't count sales income, so the club's payment can't be counted on to fund the restock.

That's why there is no restock order and no payment request on this ticket. Rent comes first, then invoice 501, then any hoodie restock. I've marked this ticket waiting on a person because the reply to the club (draft 3) needs you to review and send it. This ticket has no payment for you to approve.
next_steps: Owner: review draft 3 and send it to the Yale AI Club. It offers $52.20 per hoodie, says we're holding the 8 in stock, and gives no date yet for the other 12.
Owner: on tickets 102 and 101, approve request #2 (rent, $2,400.00, due 2026-09-02) and request #1 (invoice 501, $840.00). Approving invoice 501 lets Bulldog Print Co ship again.

Once invoice 501 is paid and there is enough cash for the restock (about $264.00 for 12 hoodies), re-run ticket 103. Accounting will then prepare a purchase order with Bulldog Print Co for your approval. The hoodies arrive 5 days after the order is placed.
After the order is placed, Customer Service drafts a follow-up with the firm arrival date for the last 12 hoodies.
If the club wants a bigger discount, go no higher than 15% ($49.30 each, 55.4% margin). If they decline, the 8 held hoodies go back on sale.
